name: Cai Qianxiang
current_role: Possibly chairman, The Great Wall of Culture Group Holding (Guangdong Great Wall Group, Chaozhou ceramics; SZSE 300089)
profile: Listed once on Hurun China 2010 (~US$150m, shared with Wu Danzhu) for 'The Grate Wall Group' (pottery). This likely refers to Guangdong Great Wall Group, a Chaozhou ceramics maker, whose chairman appears in English sources as Ting Xiang (Tingxiang) Cai; the Hurun spelling 蔡迁祥 may be a variant/typo of 蔡廷祥, which I could not confirm.
interesting_fact: MarketScreener lists Ting Xiang Cai, chairman of The Great Wall of Culture Group, as president of the Chaozhou Ceramics Industry Association and a vice president of the China Ceramics Industrial Association; he holds an MBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.
notes: Identity not confirmed: no English or Chinese source found for the exact name 蔡迁祥; match to Ting Xiang Cai is inferred from the company/industry. Very low public profile; only one Hurun appearance (2010). Verify before any outreach.

name: Nara Bhuvaneswari
current_role: Vice Chairperson & Managing Director, Heritage Foods Ltd; Managing Trustee, NTR Memorial Trust
profile: Runs Heritage Foods, the Hyderabad-based listed dairy company, which she joined in 1994 as a whole-time director before becoming Vice Chairperson & MD; she is its largest individual shareholder (~24%). She also leads the NTR Memorial Trust (healthcare, blood banks, education, clean water) and is the daughter of N. T. Rama Rao.
interesting_fact: In November 2025 she received the Institute of Directors (UK) Distinguished Fellowship in London for her social work through the NTR Trust, while Heritage Foods won the Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Corporate Governance 2025.
deep_cut_fact: She took charge of NTR Trust Bhavan in June 2014; the trust she leads runs NABH-accredited blood centres in Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati, and its NTR Sujala scheme supplies clean drinking water to about 18 lakh people in AP and Telangana.
notes: Wife of Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu; politically high-profile family, so outreach is best via Heritage Foods corporate office or NTR Trust. Heritage's site blocks some automated fetches.

name: Sharad V Parekh
profile: Co-founded Nilkamal in 1981 with elder brother Vamanrai Parekh, leaving the family's metal-button business to make plastic household goods in Powai, Mumbai. He led marketing and pioneered India's plastic material-handling (crate) business; Nilkamal is now a Rs 2,000+ cr furniture, materials-handling and retail (@home) group. He became chairman in 2020 after years as MD.
interesting_fact: Nilkamal's roots go back to a one-machine metal-button factory shed set up by the family in 1934; the brothers switched to plastics in 1981 and 'crate' became almost synonymous with the Nilkamal brand.
deep_cut_fact: Spotting that Operation Flood was spawning dairies, Sharad Parekh, then 37, followed a milk van all the way to Mumbai's Worli Dairy to pitch plastic crates; by 1983 Nilkamal won its first crate order, launching its material-handling business.
notes: Low-profile family business founder; company bio says he is active in several charitable trusts and educational institutions. Route via corporate office.

name: Rocco A Ortenzio
current_role: Deceased (October 2024); was Chairman Emeritus & Co-Founder, Select Medical
profile: Healthcare entrepreneur who founded or co-founded four healthcare companies, including Continental Medical Systems (sold to Horizon Healthcare in 1995 for $502m) and Select Medical (co-founded 1996), now a Fortune 500 company. Died October 26, 2024.
notes: Deceased: died Oct 26, 2024 per Harrisburg University tribute (https://www.harrisburgu.edu/news/2024-10-28-remembering-rocco-ortenzio/) and APTA in-memoriam notice (https://apta.org/article/2024/11/20/rocco-ortenzio-in-memoriam). Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Vincent Pilette
current_role: CEO, President & Chair of the Board, Gen Digital Inc. (Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion)
profile: Belgian-born (1972) finance executive who was CFO of Electronics for Imaging (2011) and Logitech (2013-19) before joining Symantec as CFO in 2019. He led the sale of Symantec's enterprise business, became CEO of the consumer remainder, NortonLifeLock, merged it with Avast in 2022 to form Gen Digital, and added the Board chair role in 2025.
interesting_fact: Pilette says he arrived at Symantec as CFO on the very day its CEO was fired, then led the split and sale of half the company within a year and was named CEO months later, despite never having CEO aspirations.
deep_cut_fact: As a young financial analyst at a Fortune 500 IT company he told the CFO he wanted her job; when she laid out a 15-year succession plan he left ('I don't have that much time') and chased CFO roles through 'hundreds of nos', including an initial rejection from EFI, which later hired him as CFO.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Gen press office. Has spoken publicly about CFO-to-CEO path and consumer cyber safety/AI-era scams, good podcast angles.

name: Shakuntala Agarwal
current_role: Promoter shareholder, AU Small Finance Bank Ltd (no executive or board role found)
profile: Listed by Hurun India for AU Small Finance Bank, the Jaipur-based lender founded by Sanjay Agarwal (AU Financiers, 1996) that converted to a small finance bank in 2017. AU's filings list her in the promoter group, holding ~1.86 crore shares (~2.5%) as of late 2025. No public profile, interviews or operating role found.
interesting_fact: AU's promoter group (Sanjay Agarwal, Jyoti Agarwal, Shakuntala Agarwal, MYS Holdings) built the bank from a Jaipur vehicle-finance NBFC into one of India's largest small finance banks, which has since sought RBI approval to become a universal bank.
notes: Very private passive promoter shareholder; relationship to founder Sanjay Agarwal not confirmed in sources found. Only realistic route is via AU Small Finance Bank corporate/IR office; consider approaching Sanjay Agarwal instead.

name: Ram Kripal Singh
current_role: Founder, Ram Kripal Singh Construction Pvt Ltd (RKSCPL), Ranchi, Jharkhand
profile: Founded Ram Kripal Singh Construction, a Ranchi-based contractor active since 1971 that builds government buildings, highways and bridges, stadiums, refinery and mining infrastructure for PSUs and state/central government, with ~2,500 staff. The company says it is now led by the next generation of the family.
interesting_fact: RKSCPL lists the Jharkhand Assembly Building and the JSCA International Cricket Stadium in Ranchi among its showcase projects.
deep_cut_fact: The company describes its founder's stated goal as giving 20,000 people from poor families livelihoods through its construction work.
notes: Private regional contractor; founder's current status (alive/active) not confirmed and he has no public media presence. Company is now run by the founder's sons per its website. Site warns of fraudsters impersonating the company; use only the official address.

name: Emilie Choi
current_role: President & COO, Coinbase Global; Director, Okta
profile: Johns Hopkins economics grad and Wharton MBA who started in investment banking, worked at Yahoo and on digital strategy at Warner Bros., then spent 8+ years leading M&A/corporate development at LinkedIn. Joined Coinbase in 2018 to run corporate development, became COO in 2019 and President in 2020, steering it through its 2021 listing and crypto cycles; on Okta's board since 2022.
interesting_fact: She joined Coinbase to run M&A and within a year her remit had expanded to business development, ventures, strategy, data, international and institutional coverage; she describes herself as 'not an engineer and I'm not a product person' but a partner to founders.
deep_cut_fact: She joined LinkedIn when it had about 400 employees and left when it had about 13,000; she started her tech career at Yahoo 'back when Yahoo was the epicenter of all the technology activity.'
notes: Has done several podcasts (Masters of Scale with Reid Hoffman, Grit, The Block's The Scoop), so podcast-friendly. Personal X handle not verified; LinkedIn reportedly linkedin.com/in/emiliechoi (unverified, from an aggregator).

name: Simon Mullaly
current_role: Senior Investment Executive, Blantyre Capital; Director, National CineMedia (NCMI) since Oct 2025
profile: British-born credit markets veteran (age 59 in 2025) with 25+ years in leveraged credit, restructurings and special situations at Deutsche Bank, Lehman Brothers, Goldman Sachs and Guggenheim (Head of Credit Sales & Trading, 2021-22). Joined Blantyre Capital in 2023 and sits on NCM's board as Blantyre's designee; the ~27m NCM shares reported on his Form 3 are held indirectly.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of National CineMedia, the US cinema-advertising network, as a creditor-designated director following its 2023 restructuring.
deep_cut_fact: He founded and ran Yorvik Partners, an independent niche fixed-income brokerage, until selling it in 2014; he holds a BSc (Hons) from Nottingham Trent University and a Wharton MBA.
notes: Low public profile; the large NCM stake is likely Blantyre's fund holding attributed to him, not personal wealth. Route via Blantyre Capital (London) or NCM investor relations; no published personal contact found.

name: Richard P McKenney
profile: Tufts mechanical engineer who spent 1991-2004 at GE, rising to CFO of GE Financial Assurance, then was CFO of Genworth Financial as it was spun out of GE and of Sun Life Financial. Joined Unum as CFO in 2009 and has been president and CEO since April 2015, running the Fortune 500 workplace-benefits insurer (Unum, Colonial Life; ~$13bn revenue).
interesting_fact: He trained as an engineer, not a financier: he graduated from Tufts University with a BS in mechanical engineering before joining GE in 1991 and moving into finance.
deep_cut_fact: A native of Eliot, Maine, he was a multi-sport athlete and class of 1987 valedictorian at Marshwood High School.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Unum media relations. Active in Chattanooga civic life (e.g. Siskin Hospital for Rehabilitation board per Unum bio).

name: Brian Lian
current_role: President & CEO (founder), Viking Therapeutics (NASDAQ: VKTX), San Diego
profile: Organic chemist (Whitman College BA, University of Michigan PhD, Indiana University MBA) who worked in small-molecule drug discovery at Amgen, then became a biotech equity analyst at CIBC World Markets and SunTrust Robinson Humphrey. Founded Viking in 2012, which is now developing VK2735, a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist for obesity in Phase 3 trials, in both injectable and oral forms.
interesting_fact: Viking was launched in 2014 on a broad licensing deal for five metabolic and endocrine programs from Ligand Pharmaceuticals, rather than on its own discovery science; it has since become one of the most-watched obesity-drug challengers to Novo and Lilly.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Viking while still working as a sell-side biotech analyst: he spotted metabolic drug candidates Ligand wanted to out-license, negotiated rights to five programs and got Ligand to put up about $2.5m of initial funding.

public_contacts.value: Vida Strategic Partners, Tim Brons (media): tbrons@vidasp.com

notes: Deep-cut fact comes from an aggregator profile (Fintool), so treat it with some care. Viking's 2026 contact blocks also list the CFO's company email; PR contact names rotate, so check the latest release. Ligand has disputed Viking's license for the TR-beta program (2026); avoid this topic.

name: W Blair Waltrip
current_role: Independent consultant (family & trust investments); Treasurer, National Museum of Funeral History board; retired SCI director (1986-2025)
profile: Son of SCI founder Robert L. Waltrip, he held posts at Service Corporation International, the largest US funeral and cemetery operator, from 1977 to 2000. Roles included VP corporate development, head of funeral operations, EVP of real estate, chairman & CEO of SCI's Toronto-listed Canadian subsidiary, and EVP/COO. He sat on SCI's board for 38 years before stepping down at the May 2025 annual meeting.
interesting_fact: He chose not to stand for re-election to SCI's board in 2025 after 38 years as a director; the company nominated Thad Hill to replace him.
deep_cut_fact: He serves as treasurer of the National Museum of Funeral History in Houston, which his father founded, and once ran SCI's Canadian arm as chairman & CEO when it was taken public on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
notes: Private, low-profile; no personal or office contact published. Possible routes are SCI's corporate office in Houston or the National Museum of Funeral History (his board bio is on nmfh.org).

name: Robert E Apple
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, MasTec Inc. (since Dec 2006)
profile: Naval Academy graduate and former Marine Corps lieutenant colonel who spent 1985-2004 at Hughes Electronics/DIRECTV (CEO of Hughes Electronics-Spain, COO of Telefonica's Via Digital satellite TV venture, SVP at DIRECTV). Joined MasTec in 2005 to run energy services and has been COO of the infrastructure contractor (pipelines, power delivery, communications, clean energy) since 2006; former chairman of Domtar.
interesting_fact: While on assignment from Hughes/DIRECTV Latin America he was COO and a board member of Via Digital, Telefonica's direct-broadcast satellite TV company in Spain (1997-2001).
deep_cut_fact: As a US Marine Corps aviator he graduated from the Naval Fighter Weapons School ('Top Gun') and was part of the team that rolled out the F/A-18 strike fighter.
notes: Public-company executive; no personal contact published. Route via MasTec corporate (Coral Gables, FL) or its investor relations site (investors.mastec.com). Couldn't confirm the IR/press email because the search budget ran out.

name: Richard J Tobin
current_role: Chair, President & CEO, Dover Corporation; independent director, KeyCorp
profile: Philadelphia-born (1963) former US Army officer (1985-89) with a Norwich University BA and a Drexel MBA. He held roles at GTE, Alusuisse-Lonza and Alcan, was CFO and IT head of SGS in Geneva, then CFO and CEO of CNH Global and CNH Industrial (2010-18). He has been CEO of Dover, the diversified industrial maker of pumps, refrigeration, fueling and data-center thermal equipment, since 2018.
interesting_fact: He has spent much of his career abroad, in Zurich, Montreal, Geneva and with Fiat Industrial/CNH, and was vice chairman of Türk Traktör in Ankara before returning to the US to run Dover.
deep_cut_fact: In 2014 Fiat Chrysler chairman John Elkann named Tobin as one of the managers who could eventually succeed Sergio Marchionne as FCA's CEO after 2018.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Dover corporate communications/IR (Downers Grove, IL). Dover's thermal/cooling businesses sell into data centers, a natural podcast angle. Couldn't confirm a press email because the search budget ran out. Also on the US Chamber of Commerce board.

name: Lance E D'amico
current_role: Executive Vice President, Secretary & General Counsel, Amphenol Corporation
profile: Corporate lawyer (age 57 per the 2026 proxy) who has been Amphenol's General Counsel and Secretary since 2016, SVP from 2019 and EVP from 2026, as the connector and sensor maker grew into a major supplier of AI data-center interconnect. He was previously EVP, Chief Administrative Officer & GC of logistics firm UTi Worldwide (2006-16).
interesting_fact: He has been Amphenol's top lawyer for about a decade, a period in which the company became one of the biggest beneficiaries of AI data-center buildouts through its high-speed interconnect and power products.
deep_cut_fact: Before going in-house he spent six years as an associate at Cravath, Swaine & Moore, then six years as General Counsel and EVP of Element K Corporation, an e-learning/IT-training company.
notes: Low-profile in-house counsel with no media presence; no public contact beyond Amphenol corporate/IR (Wallingford, CT). The 'interesting fact' is company context, not a personal anecdote.

name: Jonathan Mead Beaulier
current_role: Chief Revenue Officer, Snowflake Inc. (since March 31, 2026)
profile: Career enterprise-software seller (age 49 per Snowflake's 2026 proxy) who joined Snowflake in January 2016, years before its 2020 IPO, and rose through sales leadership, including VP Sales for Financial Services & Insurance (2022-24) and GVP of US Majors (2024-26). He succeeded Michael Gannon as CRO in March 2026 and now leads the AI Data Cloud company's global go-to-market.
interesting_fact: He is a rare home-grown CRO: he joined Snowflake as a seller in early 2016, when it was a small startup, and is now one of its six executive officers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied History and Economics at Colgate University (BA), not computer science or business.
notes: Newly appointed, low-profile sales executive; no public social accounts verified. Route via Snowflake IR/communications. Snowflake's website blocks automated fetches.

name: Douglas F. Bauer
current_role: CEO, Tri Pointe Homes (an indirect subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry since May 2026)
profile: Homebuilding veteran (age 64 per the 2026 proxy) who spent 1989-2009 at William Lyon Homes (Northern California division president, CFO, then President & COO). He co-founded TRI Pointe in April 2009 and has been CEO since 2013, growing it into a national builder through its IPO and the WRECO/Weyerhaeuser homebuilding merger. Sumitomo Forestry acquired Tri Pointe in May 2026, and its officers stayed on.
interesting_fact: He formed TRI Pointe in April 2009, at the bottom of the US housing crash, and took it from startup to NYSE-listed national builder before its 2026 sale to Japan's Sumitomo Forestry.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career with seven years in finance at Security Pacific National Bank in Los Angeles. He sits on the board of Building Talent Foundation, which recruits and trains construction workers, and has worked with HomeAid Orange County, which builds and renovates shelters for the temporarily homeless.
notes: Tri Pointe was delisted after the Sumitomo Forestry merger closed on May 14, 2026 (8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1561680/000119312526222960/d317054d8k.htm), so its IR inbox may be less active. I assumed he is still CEO because the officers carried over at the merger, but I could not confirm this after May 2026. University of Oregon BA, USC MBA.
